claims.text: Khartoon Weiss (TikTok, 2022) argues that brands participating in TikTok's how-to and educational content ecosystem gain product preference, not merely awareness: because the product appears as the tool solving a real functional problem in a how-to video, viewers move from consideration to preference within a single viewing experience. This mechanism converts the platform from a brand-awareness channel into a behavior-change and brand-switch channel.
claims.speaker: Khartoon Weiss
conditions: Brand content integrated into how-to or educational TikTok context
claims.mechanism: When a product is shown solving a specific functional problem in a learning context, the viewer's cognitive frame is solution-seeking rather than advertising-skepticism, so the product association is encoded as useful rather than promotional, shifting preference more durably than traditional awareness advertising.
bounded_by: Effect is strongest for products with a clear functional application; less applicable to purely image or status-driven categories

claims.text: Alex Hormozi asserts that the one-time fee name and rationale are entirely fabricated by the seller, but should be clearly communicated to the customer as something the seller is doing for them. Even if the seller never actually charges the fee (waiving it for every prospect), the mere existence of the fee functions as a discount anchor, creating perceived value equivalent to waiving a real charge.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: fee is clearly named and explained, even if fabricated
seller has flexibility to waive or charge the fee per prospect
claims.mechanism: Waiving a fee that the customer was told they would be charged creates perceived savings and goodwill without changing the actual price. The customer experiences the waived fee as a gift equivalent to its stated dollar value.
bounded_by: If the fee is never charged and the seller always waives it, it functions as a marketing frame, not actual variable pricing
Must comply with local advertising and disclosure laws

claims.text: Alex Hormozi asserts that bootstrapping constrains the types of opportunities a founder can pursue from day one: capital-intensive opportunities such as AI robotics or pharmaceutical development are functionally inaccessible without outside injection of cash.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: founder has no pre-existing personal wealth
opportunity requires large upfront capital expenditure before generating any revenue
claims.mechanism: Bootstrapped businesses must be profitable before they can reinvest, so businesses that structurally lose money for years before achieving unit-economics profitability cannot be bootstrapped from zero.
bounded_by: Low-capital opportunities such as services, agencies, B2B services, education, and dropshipping remain accessible to bootstrapped founders

claims.text: Rory Sutherland claims that important changes in consumer behavior and society happen on a 'gradually then suddenly' trajectory — they are invisible while they accumulate slowly, then appear to happen overnight at the threshold crossing; examples include the shift in English provincial city food quality and the normalization of eating out.
claims.speaker: Rory Sutherland
conditions: change is driven by behavioral normalization or network effects rather than a single event
claims.mechanism: Slow changes accumulate below the threshold of media noticeability and therefore do not trigger correction or competition; by the time they become visible they have already compounded to a decisive advantage or shift.

claims.text: Rory Sutherland argues that offering people a menu of five behavioral options and asking them to choose any two or three produces higher adoption and stronger evangelism than mandating a single universal behavior, because chosen behaviors are psychologically owned and therefore defended and promoted by the chooser.
claims.speaker: Rory Sutherland
conditions: any choice set where a moderate middle option is absent
behavioral goal is to shift population-level outcomes, not achieve 100% compliance
targeting mainstream population adoption, not early-adopter niche
where the behavior itself reveals a selfish benefit the adopter did not anticipate
claims.mechanism: The act of choosing increases hedonic valuation of the chosen behavior; people feel responsible for and satisfied with self-selected actions, whereas imposed behaviors generate resistance and zero personal advocacy.
bounded_by: Counter-signaling is an effective strategy for already-high-status individuals signaling modesty to peer groups who recognize the signal
Does not work when the problem requires universal synchronized action (e.g., drive on the left)
